hook: The goal is not to stop negative thoughts. It's to stop being afraid of them.
topic: Fear of thoughts vs. the thoughts themselves — the real target
body:
**Most approaches to negative thinking treat the thought as the problem.**

Eliminate it. Replace it. Reframe it. Think something better instead. All of these assume that if you could just clear the thought, you'd be fine.

But the thought isn't what's causing the suffering. The suffering comes from the relationship you have with the thought. From treating it as a signal that something is wrong. From believing it tells you something true and important about your situation — or about yourself.

A thought is just neural activity. It has the content it has because of the patterns your brain has built over time. It is not an instruction. It is not a verdict. It is not a prediction.

The people who manage thought spirals effectively aren't the people who never have dark thoughts. They're the people who don't grip. A thought arrives. They notice it. They don't treat it as an emergency. It passes.

Fear of the thought is the fuel. Remove the fear — or even just reduce it — and the thought has nowhere to go.

You don't need a quieter mind. You need a less frightened relationship with the one you have.

Full framework in my bio — free guide.
